note: Machine-readable compatibility ledger: every compatibility scenario is tracked as pass / known-gap / not-applicable under a permanent hc-<suite>-<capability>-<case> id. Status, reason and recordedAt semantics follow ADR-0002 section 7; the ledger was established by T11 and absorbed the T09 known-gap records (tests/compat/types/expected-divergences.json).

entries.reason: Since T25E, MAD DOM implements the attribute read/write surface (crates/mad-dom-bun/src/extensions/attributes_api.rs and js/facade/extensions/attributes.js) and every value round-trip, WebIDL DOMString argument shape and absent-name read matches happy-dom, but four genuine gaps remain. First, the T21A napi4 error degradation: a DOM-spec violation is thrown as a plain Error whose name is "Error" and which carries the frozen ERR_MAD_DOM_* code with the WHATWG name embedded in the message, while happy-dom throws a real DOMException, so error name/message differ. Second, Core validates the WHATWG Name production strictly, so a digit-led name ("1bad") is rejected with ERR_MAD_DOM_INVALID_CHARACTER while happy-dom accepts it. Third, non-Element access: MAD DOM owns the methods on Node.prototype, so a Text node's getAttribute reaches Core and throws the frozen HierarchyRequestError taxonomy, while happy-dom lacks the method on text nodes (TypeError "not a function"). Fourth, prototype layout: MAD DOM owns the methods on Node.prototype (the element's direct prototype), so getOwnPropertyDescriptor reports them present, while happy-dom inherits them from higher up the class chain (present: false).

Since T25E, MAD DOM implements the Node.textContent accessor (crates/mad-dom-bun/src/extensions/text_api.rs and js/facade/extensions/text-content.js) and every read/write, null-to-empty conversion, non-string coercion, deep-tree concatenation and text-node data round-trip matches happy-dom. Two genuine gaps remain. First, a NUL byte in the setter value: Core rejects it with ERR_MAD_DOM_INVALID_CHARACTER (text-data well-formedness, T25C) while happy-dom stores it verbatim. Second, prototype layout: MAD DOM owns the accessor on Node.prototype (the element's direct prototype), so getOwnPropertyDescriptor reports it present with a getter and a setter, while happy-dom inherits it from higher up the class chain (present: false).

Since T29, MAD DOM implements the document-structure accessors (documentElement/head/body with the implied skeleton), the innerHTML/outerHTML accessors and the T28 serializer, so document.body.appendChild(section) succeeds and the captured body outerHTML matches happy-dom byte for byte. The remaining differences are all outside T29's scope: document.querySelector is still missing (selector surface, T31), document.readyState is still undefined, the snapshot's NamedNodeMap (.attributes) and namespaceURI are not implemented yet (T34), and Element.nodeName casing differs (MAD DOM lowercases, happy-dom uppercases, T23A). First presented by the T10 real-pair runner; updated by T22/T23/T24/T25/T29; collected into the compatibility ledger by T11.

Since T23, detached Element/Text creation and the Node navigation surface match happy-dom observation for observation — nodeType, text nodeName (#text), null parent/first/last/previous/next relations, empty childNodes and per-create distinctness all record identically. The only divergence is Element.nodeName casing: MAD DOM returns the frozen lowercased tag (T23A/T23B contract) while happy-dom returns the uppercased WHATWG tag name ("div" vs "DIV"). The scenario intentionally keeps its probes detached so this ledger entry isolates the navigation contract; tree mutation is covered by dom-mutations (T24C).

Since T31, MAD DOM implements the selector/query surface (querySelector/querySelectorAll/matches/closest/getElementById, crates/mad-dom-bun/src/extensions/query_api.rs and js/facade/extensions/query.js), so the mad-dom side now counts 2 items, re-queries the same element, and finds the list through getElementById exactly like happy-dom. The remaining differences are all outside T31's scope: the events surface (addEventListener and the click propagation order — T37, mad-dom records a TypeError where happy-dom records the bubbling events), the snapshot's NamedNodeMap .attributes and namespaceURI (T34) plus the Element.nodeName casing gap (T23A), and the createWindow export shape. First presented by the T10 real-pair runner; updated by T22/T29/T31; collected into the compatibility ledger by T11.

MAD DOM still does not export CSSRule or EventPhaseEnum, and its Window is not user-constructible (it needs a genuine native handle); Document.createElement is typed (T23) but returns the minimal Element surface, so tag-name narrowing (tagName) cannot be checked yet, while querySelectorAll iteration now type-checks (T31). Updated by T22/T23/T31.

MAD DOM still does not export Event or EventPhaseEnum, and its Window is not user-constructible while its Document lacks addEventListener: listener parameter typing and enum comparison in event handlers cannot be checked yet. Updated by T22 when Window became an exported, non-constructible class.

MAD DOM does not export CustomEvent, and its Window is not user-constructible: the option-object constructor signature and the DetachedWindowAPI accessor are rejected. Updated by T22 when Window became an exported, non-constructible class.

MAD DOM does not export the Event value or the IEventInit/TEventListener type exports; annotations that reference them degrade to implicit any (TS7006) while the module-level gap exists. First recorded in T09 as div-types-type-exports; migrated into the compatibility ledger by T11.

MAD DOM's Window is not user-constructible (it requires a genuine native handle); document.body and querySelectorAll are now typed (T29/T31), so the fixture's body branch and querySelectorAll call type-check, but the remaining element/document members — id and title — are still rejected on the mad-dom target. Updated by T22/T23/T25/T29/T31.
